chunks: And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:

Everything in the sea that has a counterpart on land which is eaten is permissible to eat, and everything in the sea that has a counterpart on land whose eating is not permissible is not permissible to eat.

key_terms.أَكْلُهُ: eating it; the act whose ruling is being stated
key_terms.الْبَحْرِ: the sea; the aquatic realm being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْبَرِّ: the land; used as the basis of comparison for permissibility
key_terms.لَا يَجُوزُ: is not permissible; indicates legal prohibition

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام determine whether sea animals are halal to eat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for determining the permissibility of certain sea creatures by comparing them to their land counterparts. If the comparable land animal is halal to eat, the sea creature is also halal; if the land counterpart is not permissible, then the sea creature is likewise not permissible.
